criticity: production intent; local native PostgreSQL scope only

findings.evidence: Early implementation snapshot packages/core/src/database-policy.ts:54-55 accepts 10.0.0.0/0, fd00::/0 and invalid 10.999.999.999/32. A read-only Node regex reproduction returned true for all three. database-design.md:13 requires restrictive CIDR HBA. Lines 59 and 61 interpolate these accepted bindings into allow records before reject fallbacks.
findings.refutation: Bindings are private server configuration, so this is not an HTTP injection path. That reduces attacker control but does not establish the declared invariant: malformed or overbroad trusted configuration must fail closed rather than become a generated access policy. No claim is made that a running PostgreSQL instance accepted these noncanonical addresses; live configuration validation belongs to the pending native lab.
findings.suggestion: Parse actual IPv4/IPv6 networks and require canonical network masks fully contained in the authorized private range; reject malformed octets and masks escaping that range before generating HBA. Add negative compiler/native checks.

evidence.result: Independent cluster/PGDATA/WAL and weaker native laboratory boundary are explicit; no Docker fallback, remote qualification or provider-enabled-by-default path is authorized. E03 depends on completed local E02.S03.
One FoundationEngine supplies admission, locks, grants, epochs, fencing, reservations and uncertainty handling. Identity mismatch must quarantine rather than adopt or delete a foreign cluster.
Private bootstrap material, runtime role restrictions, per-owner default privileges, SCRAM/verify-full TLS and negative cross-cell/privilege/transport tests preserve the constitution at design level.
AC-27 through AC-34 have named future test IDs and observable positive/negative behavior. Unsupported runtime, backup, export and restore capabilities remain unavailable rather than claimed complete.

implementation_checks.result: The current binding uses the same CIDRs for service roles and bootstrap TCP access to all databases. This is a concrete lack of admin-source separation, but not a confirmed credential escalation: HBA still requires the bootstrap credential, and the design does not categorically ban private administrative TCP. For non-loopback deployment, require separately authorized admin sources (or no admin TCP); Windows native lab may explicitly use loopback-only admin access. Do not claim this early snapshot implements a separate admin network boundary.

Final audit must inspect every creating owner/default ACL, effective grants including PUBLIC template databases, TLS client hostname checks, independent effective configuration and resource limits. max_wal_size alone cannot certify a filesystem WAL quota.
